basis: Ingested fungal toxins cause gastrointestinal toxicity; other target organs vary by toxin. Definition describes poisoning, not fungal infection.
Plasma cell neoplasm; approximately 80% arise in upper respiratory sites, including nasopharynx, sinuses and larynx. Other sites are minorities.
Malignant vascular neoplasm originating in the aorta.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Cystine storage disease defined by renal and ocular injury; rickets occurs in 80-99%. Neurologic abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Benign ovarian reproductive stromal neoplasm; endocrine dysfunction is not established across this group.
T-cell immunodeficiency with defining disseminated HPV-associated cutaneous lesions; lymphoma is a reported complication, not common involvement.
Chronic intertwin transfusion produces defining donor anemia and recipient polycythemia; fetal blood involvement supplies an axis despite obstetric context.
Recurrent respiratory infections in 13/13; chronic diarrhea indicates intestinal dysfunction in 5/13 (~38%). Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Benign polypoid lesion occupying the middle ear.
Age-related opacity of the lens nucleus.
Immune-mediated Crohn inflammation of the jejunum and ileum; no additional organ meets the common direct-injury threshold.
Neurodevelopmental disease with cerebellar hypoplasia and seizures; contractures in 3/3 and 5/5 assessed. Visual impairment is predominantly cerebral.
Carcinoma originating in the distal common bile duct; extrahepatic bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Benign vaginal epithelial neoplasm confined to a reproductive organ; definition explicitly excludes an HPV relationship.
Neoplasm originating in or occupying the esophagus.
Dermatophyte infection of beard hair and associated skin.
IFNAR2-related immunodeficiency; reported vaccine-associated measles does not establish common direct injury to another organ.
Epilepsy defined by antibody-mediated immune dysfunction of the brain.
Benign epithelial tumor of the reproductive rete testis, without defined endocrine involvement.
Prostate epithelial carcinoma; reproductive origin has no axis. Urinary invasion or metastatic injury is not intrinsic to this histologic variant.
Eye and skeletal abnormalities define WMS; persistent skin thickening and structural cardiovascular abnormalities each occur in 30-79% per HPO.
Definition specifies impaired blood glucose regulation with hyperglycemia; the malabsorption parent does not establish intestinal disease.
Inherited cerebellar degeneration with ataxia; tinnitus in 3/7 is a symptom without established ear injury. Abnormal saccades are neurologic.
Meningeal tumor of the central nervous system; psammoma bodies define its histologic subtype.
